findings.Quote: The corn on both sides of the 88 was very still.
findings.Note: Purpose calls for CJ closing comms, Hauser's channel going to static, and the standoff framing; instead the beat ends mid-sentence on the burial/tamping action and never delivers the stated beats (comms closing, static, Eigenlift/sky framing, the no-fire standoff).
findings.Fix: Extend the beat through CJ closing comms and Hauser going to static, with the machine framed against the tower and sky.

findings.Quote: the hairs on his forearms lifting, his stomach dropping half an inch
findings.Note: Stacked stock physiological shorthand for awe/dread rather than a specific observed reaction.
findings.Fix: Cut to one concrete detail, e.g. just the throat tightening, and let the sound do the work.

findings.Quote: The tine comes down on the man who was in the way. The threat-wail starts
findings.Note: Purpose specifies the tine strike and threat-wail onset as the beat's climax, but the excerpt cuts off before either occurs — the prose ends on 'His hand moved. The' without depicting the stated events.
findings.Fix: Extend excerpt or confirm the tine strike and wail are rendered on-page within this beat.

findings.Quote: He'd been on the hull all day and still couldn't have said which.
findings.Note: Purpose specifies this beat centers on Wes coming down and CJ placing Pip beside the machine for the dog's territorial comedy beat undercutting the sacred moment; instead most of the text lingers on Wes's descent and the machine's departure, and cuts off before Pip's mark-territory payoff or CJ's report are shown.
findings.Fix: Compress the descent/departure material and land firmly on Pip sniffing the tine and marking it against the machine's stillness.

findings.Quote: and now he did what he did at every stop that matte
findings.Note: Beat cuts off before the comedic payoff (lifting his leg) and before CJ's report/recommendation, which the purpose requires.
findings.Fix: Complete the sentence and add CJ's filed report language: behavioral anomaly, origin unknown, threat level zero, recommendation to leave the machine in place.

findings.Quote: the whole carapace tilted forward like a ship taking on water
findings.Note: Ship-taking-on-water is a stock disaster simile that doesn't add anything specific to a forty-ton farm machine's posture.
findings.Fix: Describe the tilt in mechanical terms specific to the machine's own anatomy instead.

findings.Quote: Find the fault. Put a word to it.
findings.Note: Reads as a slightly on-the-nose internal-rule aphorism rather than lived detail.
findings.Fix: Cut one of the two restatements; let the rule appear once.

findings.Quote: It was the way a sound changes when the shape of the room around it changes.
findings.Note: Vague sound-simile that doesn't clarify what actually changed in the wail; explains nothing concrete.
findings.Fix: Replace with a specific acoustic detail (pitch, resonance, duration) rather than an abstract analogy.

findings.Quote: patient, like something that had been doing this for years
findings.Note: Filler qualifier stating an obvious inference rather than showing a specific gait detail.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; the preceding mechanical description already implies routine.

findings.Quote: And Behemoths came from somewhere. All of them. Always.
findings.Note: Reads as a pseudo-profound aphorism/filler assertion rather than advancing CJ's actual reasoning about the missing registry.
findings.Fix: Cut, or replace with a concrete procedural detail about what an unregistered unit implies for her protocol.

findings.Quote: a view of the Rock River that was genuinely good if you were somebody who needed that from a posting
findings.Note: Wry throwaway phrasing that reads as authorial quip rather than grounded characterization.
findings.Fix: Trim to a plainer statement of the view and let 'CJ had stopped needing it' carry the irony.

findings.Quote: Forty feet was not very far.
findings.Note: Flat filler-aphorism beat that states the obvious instead of building tension.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or replace with a concrete sensory detail (e.g., the sound of the units closing).

findings.Quote: the smallest arc needed to make the obstacle not be there
findings.Note: Reads as an aphoristic label for the machine's efficiency rather than observed action; slightly on-the-nose 'profound' phrasing.
findings.Fix: Ground it in a specific physical beat instead of the abstracted 'obstacle not be there' construction.

findings.Quote: the kind of loud that tears the throat
findings.Note: Vague intensifier standing in for concrete sensory detail — tells rather than shows the strain.
findings.Fix: Describe the specific physical sensation, e.g., 'his voice cracked on the second word.'

findings.Quote: A pause. Not frustration — accounting.
findings.Note: Tells the reader how to interpret Hauser's tone rather than letting dialogue/action convey it; borders on authorial explanation.
findings.Fix: Cut the interpretive clause and let the clipped dialogue carry the characterization.

findings.Quote: and while she watched it the shape of the thing came together. The machine wasn't walking toward
findings.Note: Purpose specifies the beat should land on the reveal of open farmland and Eigenlift towers rising from the corn, but the excerpt cuts off before that image appears.
findings.Fix: Confirm the towers/GLMZ description follows immediately; if not, the beat as excerpted doesn't deliver the stated visual payoff.

findings.Quote: the kind of dog that looks put together specifically to be hard to stop once it has somewhere to be
findings.Fix: cut the aphoristic framing; describe the physical build instead

findings.Quote: He just let himself be lifted, the way you let yourself be lifted when you've been moving forty miles and your body has said everything it has to say.
findings.Note: circular, tautological phrasing that tells rather than shows exhaustion
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete physical beat — muscles slack, no resistance in the spine

findings.Quote: the loose full commitment of a dog who'd looked the situation over and found it acceptable
findings.Note: cute anthropomorphizing aphorism, slightly undercuts the exhaustion just established
findings.Fix: trim to physical description without the judgment clause

findings.Quote: He was the kind of man who read a situation once and then waited it out.
findings.Note: summary character aphorism, tells rather than shows
findings.Fix: cut or replace with an action beat that demonstrates the trait

findings.Quote: "You can find me," he said. "When this is done."
findings.Note: beat purpose doesn't call for a dangling mystery hook; slightly diffuses the focused handoff-and-race-back structure the beat promises
findings.Fix: either cut or ground the line so it doesn't read as an unearned tease

findings.Quote: The corn on both sides of the 88 was very still.
findings.Note: Stillness-of-nature-as-tension beat is a stock atmospheric cue.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in a more specific sensory detail.

findings.Quote: The way you pack earth around a fence post when you mean for it to hold through the freeze and the thaw.
findings.Note: Explanatory simile drifts into folksy narrator-aphorism territory rather than observed action.
findings.Fix: Trim to the concrete action without the didactic gloss.

findings.Quote: Long enough that Wes counted his own pulse against it — past forty beats, maybe sixty.
findings.Note: Counting-heartbeats-as-tension-marker is a familiar device bordering on the heartbeat-in-throat cliché family.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, non-biometric marker of elapsed time.

findings.Quote: He went down the way the machine had gone all day: deliberate, unhurried, because hurrying was how you fell.
findings.Note: Aphoristic explanatory tag ('because hurrying was how you fell') states an obvious universal truth rather than showing character-specific detail.
findings.Fix: Cut the because-clause; let the action imply the caution.
